arxiv-2111-07551.title: On the Complexity of Inverse Semigroup Conjugacy Thanks: This work was partially supported by the Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (Portuguese Foundation for Science and Technology) through the projects UIDB/00297/2020 (Centro de Matemática e Aplicações) and PTDC/MAT-PUR/31174/2017.
arxiv-2111-07551.creator: Trevor Jack
arxiv-2111-07551.description: Abstract . We investigate the computational complexity of various decision problems related to conjugacy in finite inverse semigroups. We describe polynomial-time algorithms for checking if two elements in such a semigroup are ∼ p \sim_{p} conjugate and whether an inverse monoid is factorizable. We describe a connection between checking ∼ i \sim_{i} conjugacy and checking membership in inverse semigroups.

arxiv-2205-10784.title: Fully symmetric nonequilibrium response of stochastic systems
arxiv-2205-10784.creator: David Andrieux
arxiv-2205-10784.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by David Andrieux. We show that the nonequilibrium response of Markovian dynamics can be made fully symmetric, both near and far from equilibrium. This is achieved by varying the affinities along equivalence classes in the space of stochastic dynamics. Context and objectives Nonequilibrium response theory has long been studied near equilibrium, where general results such as the fluctuation-dissipation theorem or the Onsager reciprocity relations hold.

arxiv-2206-14736.title: Optimal light cone and digital quantum simulation of interacting bosons
arxiv-2206-14736.creator: Tomotaka Kuwahara 1,2, Tan Van Vu 3, Keiji Saito 3
arxiv-2206-14736.description: Abstract The speed limit of information propagation is one of the most fundamental features in non-equilibrium physics. The region of information propagation by finite-time dynamics is approximately restricted inside the effective light cone that is formulated by the Lieb-Robinson bound.

arxiv-2307-01297.title: Tensor Sandwich: Tensor Completion for Low CP-Rank Tensors via Adaptive Random Sampling
arxiv-2307-01297.creator: Cullen Haselby, Santhosh Karnik, Mark Iwen
arxiv-2307-01297.description: Abstract We propose an adaptive and provably accurate tensor completion approach based on combining matrix completion techniques (see, e.g., [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] ) for a small number of slices with a modified noise robust version of Jennrich’s algorithm (see, e.g., [ 4 , Section 3] ).

arxiv-2409-02873.title: Bounds on detection of Bell correlations with entangled ultra-cold atoms in optical lattices under occupation defects
arxiv-2409-02873.creator: T. Hernández Yanes ∗, Y. Bamaara ∗, A. Sinatra, E. Witkowska
arxiv-2409-02873.description: Abstract Bell non-locality stems from quantum correlations effectively identified using inequalities. Spin chains, simulated with ultra-cold atoms in optical lattices, Rydberg atoms in tweezer arrays, trapped ions, or molecules, allow single-spin control and measurement. Therefore, they are suitable for studying fundamental aspects of these correlations and non-locality.

arxiv-2511-22385.title: Logic of (Common or Distributed) ∗ Knowledge
arxiv-2511-22385.creator: Chenwei Shi
arxiv-2511-22385.description: Abstract In this paper, we generalize epistemic logic so that it can help reason about ways of combining common knowledge and distributed knowledge such as “common distributed knowledge”, “distributed common knowledge”, “distributed common distributed knowledge” and so on. Moreover, we study the logic of its dynamic update by arbitrary reading events.

arxiv-2512-03237.title: LLM-Guided Material Inference for 3D Point Clouds
arxiv-2512-03237.creator: Nafiseh Izadyar, Teseo Schneider
arxiv-2512-03237.description: Abstract Most existing 3D shape datasets and models focus solely on geometry, overlooking the material properties that determine how objects appear. We introduce a two-stage large language model (LLM) based method for inferring material composition directly from 3D point clouds with coarse segmentations.

pmc-11403870.title: Mining impactful discoveries from the biomedical literature
pmc-11403870.creator: Erwan Moreau, Orla Hardiman, Mark Heverin, Declan O’Sullivan
pmc-11403870.description: BackgroundLiterature-based discovery (LBD) aims to help researchers to identify relations between concepts which are worthy of further investigation by text-mining the biomedical literature. While the LBD literature is rich and the field is considered mature, standard practice in the evaluation of LBD methods is methodologically poor and has not progressed on par with the domain.

pmc-11492256.title: Ash Interaction with Two Cu-Based Magnetic Oxygen Carriers during Biomass Combustion by the Chemical Looping with Oxygen Uncoupling Process
pmc-11492256.creator: A. Filsouf, I. Adánez-Rubio, T. Mendiara, A. Abad, J. Adánez
pmc-11492256.description: Chemical-looping combustion (CLC) stands out as a promising method for carbon capture and storage for the purpose of mitigating climate change. The process involves the conversion of fuel facilitated by an oxygen carrier, with the resulting CO2 inherently separated from other air components. Notably, when applied to biomass combustion this process offers a pathway to achieving negative CO2 emissions.

pmc-11691303.title: NICOTINAMIDE RIBOSIDE SUPPLEMENTATION PROTECTS AGAINST VIRAL-INDUCED NEURODEGENERATION IN AGED MICE
pmc-11691303.creator: Daniel Enterria-Morales, Anais Claire Gonzalez, Bianca Jallorina, Adrian Martinez, Andrew Doan, Aadit Karve, Mikaela Joya, Matthew Shtrahman
pmc-11691303.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Several lines of research support the hypothesis that boosting cellular nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) may induce metabolic adaptation that helps neurons maintain healthy function as they age and slow neurodegeneration, making this approach a promising therapy for neuroregeneration. To prove this strategy, we tested the ability of Nicotinamide Riboside (NR), a pyridine-nucleoside precursor to NAD+, to prevent neuronal cell loss in a model of viral induced neurodegeneration using recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV).

pmc-12443424.title: Suppression of Aedes albopictus in Sri Lanka using the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) with a sustained effect
pmc-12443424.creator: Menaka Hapugoda, Nilmini Silva Gunawardene, Tharaka Ranathunge, Sudath Samaraweera, K. Karunathilake, Bazoumana B.D. Sow, Gayan Parakrama Withanage, Indika Weerasinghe, Hamidou Maiga, Jeremy Bouyer
pmc-12443424.description: Dengue fever remains a significant public health concern in Sri Lanka, leading to recurrent epidemics and imposing substantial socio-economic burdens. This study aimed to assess the efficacy of the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) against Aedes albopictus (Skuse), the predominant dengue vector in the country, through a pilot field trial of an Integrated Vector Management (IVM) strategy including the SIT.

pmc-13126625.title: SAFR: Enabling Fragment-Based Drug Discovery with a Synthetic Binding Pose Data Set
pmc-13126625.creator: Joan Cabot-March, Xavier Jalencas, Jordi Mestres
pmc-13126625.description: Fragment-Based Drug Discovery (FBDD) is a powerful strategy with a proven track record of generating potent bioactive small molecules from low-affinity chemical fragments. Computational approaches to FBDD are often limited by the availability of high-quality, structurally resolved data on fragment binding poses.

pmc-13429638.title: Single-cell analysis reveals KLF10-high macrophages induced by glioblastoma cells are associated with tumor progression
pmc-13429638.creator: Xiaodong Zhang, Caiping Chen, Qianya Fan, Sheng Chen, Duanzheng Cao, Zhonglin Hu, Yejun Zhou, Jinfang Xu, Delin Wang
pmc-13429638.description: BackgroundGlioblastoma (GBM) is the most common and aggressive primary malignant tumor of the adult central nervous system, with nearly 90% of cases recurring within two years despite standard surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) play critical roles in GBM recurrence, but their characteristics in recurrent GBM remain insufficiently defined.

pmc-13537854.title: A Bayesian bivariate spatial modeling framework for stage-specific cancer incidence and targeting of screening efforts
pmc-13537854.creator: Qinyun Lin, Carl Bonander, Ulf Strömberg
pmc-13537854.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Geographic differences in cancer stage at diagnosis may reflect both variation in underlying cancer risk and variation in the extent of early detection through screening or other diagnostic testing. Mapping both late-stage incidence (as an indicator of disease burden) and late-minus-early difference (as an indicator of insufficient diagnostic activity relative to the underlying disease burden) provides an empirically grounded way to identify small areas (neighborhoods) where enhanced early detection may yield the greatest benefits.
